correctness.rationale: Normalize the 3xN Fourier frame to Parseval; rephase each erased column to obtain a real symmetric Gram with diagonal 3 and Dirichlet-kernel offdiagonals. The retained lower bound is 1 minus the erased Gram largest eigenvalue/N. Diagonalize the consecutive Gram by midpoint symmetry for the exact radical. For N>=8, strict Perron–Frobenius monotonicity for the nonnegative absolute-value comparison proves every nonconsecutive triple loses. For N=7, a strict elementary radical inequality separates every other three-set; for N=6, explicit pairwise-kernel values yield strict separation. Finally, any three retained distinct Fourier columns form a nonsingular Vandermonde matrix, giving strict positivity for N>=6. Independent numerical Jacobi diagonalization corroborates all 211861 masks over N=6..48 but is not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: A three-frequency Parseval harmonic frame is a natural oversampled Fourier sensing system. Exactly three worst-case lost sensor readings form the first geometry with a genuinely 3x3 sign-changing Dirichlet Gram, so exact minimax lower-frame stability and a full N-mask optimizer classification have direct mathematical and robustness meaning. Strict all-order comparison and exceptional low-order regimes supply substantive structure beyond an evaluation on one selected erasure pattern. The result does not purport to solve arbitrary erasure counts or noise-decoder optimization.
